raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`DecodeCudaGraphRunner._init_replay_attn_metadata` only routes the attention-metadata prep through the metadata glue graph when `raw_bs == bs`. Every other replay runs the eager `init_forward_metadata_out_graph` path, which is dozens of small host-dispatched ops. Two common cases hit that path:
- The DSpark draft runner is dp-local, so it replays at the capture bucket of its own batch size. Any rank whose batch is not exactly a capture size takes the eager path.
- Target verify replays padded to the DP max take it as well.

On DSV4.1-Flash GB300 disagg DEP16 (c2884, 40 running per rank), the draft `G.attn_meta` costs 0.56-0.62 ms on padded ranks vs 0.06 ms glued. That cost sits on the host path between the DP agreement and the draft graph launch.

## Related PRs

One of four DSV4.1 attn-DP decode host-path changes that cut the host work between the DP agreement and the draft graph launch. They are independent in code and were measured together: #47676 (padded metadata glue), #47677 (persistent DP-MoE counts), #47678 (bulk decode-prep fill) and #47685 (KV page top-up, measured on top of the other three).

## Modifications

The glue route now also takes padded replays (`0 < raw_bs < bs`). There is no separate switch: it engages wherever the backend declared the DSV4 draft or target-verify glue (the audited host-free prep) and the runner is not in ragged verify mode, and falls back to the eager prep otherwise. Non-DSV4 backends, the generic `SGLANG_ENABLE_METADATA_GLUE_GRAPH` glue, TBO and LoRA keep the padding-free route.

Behavior change: the DSpark draft glue is on by default (static ragged verify mode), so padded draft replays now take the glue graph without any flag. The target-verify glue still follows `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_VERIFY_METADATA_GLUE`. The DEP16 / DEP32 validation below ran without `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` on decode, i.e. in exactly this default configuration; the TP4 c1 runs had it on.

Why the padded prep is the same as the eager padded prep: both read the same `req_pool_indices` / `seq_lens` slots, whose tails `fill_from` resets to the registry pad values (0 and `seq_len_fill_value`). The glue view reads the padded `out_cache_loc` slot (`num_tokens` is passed for every glued replay). `fill_from` zeroed that slot's tail, and the eager prep zero-pads the raw tensor to the same length. The declared prep reads nothing else that depends on `raw_bs`, so the captured prep for key `bs` serves padded and unpadded replays alike. IDLE replays stay eager. The contract comment in `metadata_glue_graph.py` is updated to cover the padded route.

All runs: GB300, DSV4.1-Flash, on a 2026-10-30 nightly.

## Accuracy Tests

- In-server bitwise check (diagnostic overlay, not part of this PR): for the first 40 captured padded draft replays per rank, the check snapshots the glued metadata, runs the eager padded prep on the same inputs, and compares every metadata tensor (page_table, raw_out_loc, seq_lens_casual, positions_casual, swa_page_indices, swa_topk_lengths). Result on DEP16: 640 checks (16 ranks, raw_bs 2-13 on bs=14), 0 mismatches.
- The padded target-verify route is covered by the same argument, but none of the runs below exercised it: it needs `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_VERIFY_METADATA_GLUE`, which was off in the DEP runs, and TP4 c1 never pads.
- GSM8K, 1P1D DEP16 with real DSpark acceptance, together with the two sibling host changes (#47677, #47678): 96.82% (1319 examples, 0% truncated or errors) vs 96.89% without them. Accept length 3.50 vs 3.49-3.51.
- TP4 c1 agg (mega flag on, all three host changes): T=1 GSM8K 97.33% vs 97.33%, long-context needle retrieval at 20K-160K tokens 48/48 vs 48/48 (greedy) and 24/24 vs 24/24 (T=1), accept length 3.591 vs 3.598.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| | DEP16 nsys, before | DEP16 nsys, after |
|---|---|---|
| draft `G.attn_meta`, median over ranks | 170 us | 58 us |
| draft `G.attn_meta`, worst rank | 620 us | 64 us |

The following numbers are **combined** with the two sibling host changes (#47677 DSpark persistent DP-MoE counts, #47678 DFlash bulk decode prep). Same cluster and recipe, but the two arms ran on different days:
- DEP32 c5768 (10P1D): decode step p50 13.9 ms vs 15.2 ms. This is the robust number.
- Same runs: steady-window per-GPU throughput (prompt + completion tokens, mean of minutes 8-20 of the aiperf run, same x0.96 normalisation for both arms) 660.6k vs 664.4k tok/s/GPU at p90 interactivity 219.8 vs 200.8 tok/s/user (+9.5%). Same-day controls of this recipe drift by about 3% on interactivity, so read the interactivity gain as indicative, not exact.
- DEP16 c2884: 720.1k vs 719.0k tok/s/GPU (same steady-window metric and normalisation), step 13.73 vs 13.80 ms (no regression).
- TP4 c1 agg: step p50 3.514 vs 3.501 ms, p90 interactivity 968.1 vs 963.2 tok/s/user (neutral).

A MegaMoE NVLink barrier timeout after the benchmark abort also happens without these changes, so it is not caused by them. Serving-phase results are unaffected.

## Checklist
- [x] Format with pre-commit
- [x] GPU validation on cluster (above)
- [x] Unit tests: test_dsv41_draft_metadata_glue.py, test_dsv41_target_verify_metadata_glue.py and test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py (existing tests updated for the `num_tokens` argument, a padded-slot case, and the padded / IDLE routing cases)

@@ -271,6 +271,7 @@ class DecodeCudaGraphRunner(BaseCudaGraphRunner):
     # Set in __init__: which DSpark runner's prep the glue graph serves past the guard.
     _draft_metadata_glue = False
     _target_metadata_glue = False
+    _padded_glue = False
     _metadata_prep_fork: Optional[tuple] = None
     _metadata_prep_fork_resolved = False
     _early_verify_metadata = None
@@ -607,6 +608,9 @@ def __init__(
                 self.device, strict=envs.SGLANG_IS_IN_CI.get()
             )
         self._skip_glued_replay_view = envs.SGLANG_OPT_SKIP_GLUED_REPLAY_VIEW.get()
+        self._padded_glue = (
+            self._draft_metadata_glue or self._target_metadata_glue
+        ) and not self.ragged_verify_mode
         # SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_TARGET_METADATA_EARLY: the verify's inputs and metadata glue
         # graph run on a side stream beside the draft graph (stage_verify_metadata_early).
         self._early_verify_metadata: Optional[EarlyVerifyMetadata] = (
@@ -1719,7 +1723,7 @@ def _init_replay_attn_metadata(
         glue_route = (
             self._metadata_glue is not None
             and not self._metadata_glue.disabled
-            and raw_bs == bs
+            and (raw_bs == bs or (self._padded_glue and 0 < raw_bs < bs))
             and not self.enable_two_batch_overlap
             and self.model_runner.lora_manager is None
         )
@@ -1777,7 +1781,7 @@ def _init_replay_attn_metadata_from_view(
                 cast(ForwardBatch, fb_view)
             )
         if glue_key is not None:
-            self._glue_draft_inputs(fb_view)
+            self._glue_draft_inputs(fb_view, num_tokens)
             with self._prep_attention_variant(attention_variant):
                 self._metadata_glue.run(attn_backend, fb_view, glue_key)
         else:
@@ -1944,14 +1948,14 @@ def _maybe_log_draft_glue(self) -> None:
                 glue.eager,
             )
 
-    def _glue_draft_inputs(self, fb_view) -> None:
+    def _glue_draft_inputs(self, fb_view, num_tokens: int) -> None:
         """The draft glue graph reads its inputs by address: out_cache_loc from the
-        registry slot fill_from just wrote, not the step's own (fresh) tensor."""
+        registry slot fill_from just wrote, not the step's own (fresh) tensor. A
+        padded replay reads the whole padded slot (fill_from zeroed its tail)."""
         if (
             self._draft_metadata_glue or self._target_metadata_glue
         ) and fb_view.out_cache_loc is not None:
-            n = fb_view.out_cache_loc.shape[0]
-            fb_view.out_cache_loc = self.buffers.out_cache_loc[:n]
+            fb_view.out_cache_loc = self.buffers.out_cache_loc[:num_tokens]
 
     def execute(
         self,

@@ -11,9 +11,11 @@
 
 Correctness contract:
 
-- The caller only routes here when the replay is padding-free
-  (raw_bs == padded bs) and TBO / LoRA are off, so every
-  Python-visible branch inside the backends is constant per key.
+- The caller only routes here when TBO / LoRA are off and the replay is
+  padding-free (raw_bs == padded bs) or, outside ragged verify mode, a padded
+  replay of a backend-declared DSV4 glue whose prep reads only the padded
+  slots; so every Python-visible branch inside the backends is constant per
+  key.
 - Python side effects (each backend's ``forward_metadata`` object) are
   snapshotted at capture time and re-installed on every replay; the graph
   replays only the device ops that refresh the tensors those objects point to.

@@ -667,10 +667,13 @@ class TestReplayAttnMetadataWiring(CustomTestCase):
 
     KEY = (2, "TARGET_VERIFY", "TARGET_VERIFY")
 
-    def _replay(self, glue, *, raw_bs=2, bs=2, skip=True, staged=False):
+    def _replay(
+        self, glue, *, raw_bs=2, bs=2, skip=True, staged=False, padded_glue=False
+    ):
         runner = mod.DecodeCudaGraphRunner.__new__(mod.DecodeCudaGraphRunner)
         runner._metadata_glue = glue
         runner._skip_glued_replay_view = skip
+        runner._padded_glue = padded_glue
         runner.enable_two_batch_overlap = False
         runner.model_runner = SimpleNamespace(lora_manager=None)
         runner.capture_forward_mode = mod.ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY
@@ -722,6 +725,15 @@ def test_replay_routes(self):
         views, eager = self._replay(glue, raw_bs=1)
         self.assertEqual((glue.calls, eager), ([], views))
 
+        # A declared DSV4 glue also takes padded replays; IDLE (raw_bs 0) stays eager.
+        glue = _RecordingGlue(captured_keys=[key])
+        views, eager = self._replay(glue, raw_bs=1, padded_glue=True)
+        self.assertEqual((glue.calls, views, eager), ([("replay", key)], [], []))
+
+        glue = _RecordingGlue(captured_keys=[key])
+        views, eager = self._replay(glue, raw_bs=0, padded_glue=True)
+        self.assertEqual((glue.calls, eager), ([], views))
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

@@ -134,15 +134,17 @@ def test_the_glue_reads_the_registry_slot(self):
         step_own = torch.arange(100, 106)
         view = SimpleNamespace(out_cache_loc=step_own)
         runner._draft_metadata_glue = False
-        runner._glue_draft_inputs(view)
+        runner._glue_draft_inputs(view, 6)
         self.assertIs(view.out_cache_loc, step_own)
         runner._draft_metadata_glue = True
-        runner._glue_draft_inputs(view)
+        runner._glue_draft_inputs(view, 6)
         slot = view.out_cache_loc
         self.assertEqual(slot.data_ptr(), runner.buffers.out_cache_loc.data_ptr())
         self.assertEqual(slot.shape, step_own.shape)
+        runner._glue_draft_inputs(view, 8)
+        self.assertEqual(view.out_cache_loc.shape, (8,))
         idle = SimpleNamespace(out_cache_loc=None)
-        runner._glue_draft_inputs(idle)
+        runner._glue_draft_inputs(idle, 0)
         self.assertIsNone(idle.out_cache_loc)

@@ -100,7 +100,7 @@ def test_the_target_glue_reads_the_registry_slot(self):
         runner.buffers = SimpleNamespace(out_cache_loc=torch.arange(16))
         view = SimpleNamespace(out_cache_loc=torch.arange(100, 106))
         runner._draft_metadata_glue, runner._target_metadata_glue = False, True
-        runner._glue_draft_inputs(view)
+        runner._glue_draft_inputs(view, 6)
         self.assertEqual(
             view.out_cache_loc.data_ptr(), runner.buffers.out_cache_loc.data_ptr()
         )
